title: Rosa brings in the harvest
topic: A farmer named Rosa brings in the wheat harvest: the combine cuts the field, sacks of grain go onto a trailer, clouds gather, the family works until evening, Rosa closes the gate
tail_E: The next morning the miller grinds the first sacks of grain into fine white
target_note: 'flour' is predictable only from the harvest context (wheat, grain, sacks): a miller grinding grain produces flour, and 'fine white' narrows the completion to it. The word does not occur in the units or the tail, and neither does its German equivalent 'Mehl'. ' flour' is a single Pythia token (id 12274). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' flour') = 0.16 on the all-English rendering, rank 1 (next: ' bread' 0.06); still rank 1 (p = 0.21) on the K=2 C1 rendering.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (DEV04A, farmer Rosa, development family)
notes: Development family (dose/threshold choice only, never for confirmation). Ten units: Rosa begins the harvest at sunrise; the wheat sways in the wind; her brother drives the combine across the field; the machine cuts the stalks; Rosa fills sacks with grain; two helpers load the sacks onto a trailer; the tractor pulls the trailer to the farm; dark clouds gather over the hills; the whole family works until late; Rosa closes the gate after a long day. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Rosa), other people (her brother, two helpers - plural, the whole family) and objects (the wheat, the machine, the tractor, dark clouds - plural), so that C3 switches cross singular and plural subject-verb agreement; units 2, 8 and 9 have bare intransitive predicates (sways/wiegt sich, gather/sammeln sich, works/arbeitet). Unit 6 'laden ... auf einen Anhänger' is the simple verb 'laden' with a directional PP (not the separable 'aufladen'); unit 8 uses 'sammeln sich' instead of the separable 'ziehen auf'. No separable verbs. Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Units 1 and 10 read naturally in English, unit 9 in German; unit 10 closes the day.
